learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire knowledge about the basic concepts of automatisms and basic control methods, as well as for solving real problems and basic automation projects.

syllabus_topics: Lab Practice P1 - Introduction to programming of logic automatisms with PLC LOGO
Lab Practice P2 - Automatisms with timers and counters in PLC LOGO
Lab Practice P3 - Programming of sequential logic automatisms with PLC LOGO
Lab Practice P4 - Introduction to Simulink: Simulation of a DC servomotor (I)
Lab Practice P5 - Introduction to Simulink: Simulation of a DC servomotor (II)
Lab Practice P6 - Steady-state response analysis
Lab Practice P7 - PID controller design: Speed and elevation of a parabolic antenna motor
Influence of other factors on Frequency Response

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative/eliminatory partial exams (AE1)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final exam (AE1) contributes 75%, requires a minimum score of 5/10 to pass, and is recoverable in the extraordinary call. Lab practice questionnaires (AE2) contribute 25%, are graded as an average weighted by attendance, and are not recoverable. If AE1 is not passed, the final course grade will be the minimum between 4 and the weighted average of AE1 and AE2 (0.75 * AE1 + 0.25 * AE2). Global assessment involves a written exam (75%) and a practical exam (25%), following similar passing conditions and the same grade calculation if the written exam is not passed.
